column1: # The Linux renderer's frames, drawn by wgpu 29.0.3's Vulkan backend (the
# `wgpu-oracle` build's arm on the same Mesa as the first-party GL arm, the
# differential GL was held to until GW.6; docs/AUDIT-third-party-2026-10-15.md)
# in the Linux lane's guest (`targo --unverified lab linux`), with the guest's
# monospace face and Noto Color Emoji, before wgpu left the workspace: the
# first 100 rows per architecture on the devendor/gw6 branch, 2026-10-26, and
# the three video/take rows (the video tap's frames, which the deleted GL
# video differential compared) on devendor/gw6-rec the same day, on the same
# guest, the first 100 drawn again identically. No EDR, blit or crown rows:
# the GL arm has no half-float present, and those runners are Metal's.
# One block per architecture and adapter, the adapter GL's renderer string:
# llvmpipe on aarch64 and on x86_64 under Rosetta (lavapipe drew them). The
# GPU instance (`lab linux --gpu`, zink on Venus) has no block: two runs of
# wgpu on Venus there drew 36 of the first 100 frames differently, readbacks
# holding a neighbouring frame's bytes, so nothing repeatable could be
# recorded. Every row was drawn by wgpu; a stated re-record names its rows and
# its drawer here. src/frame_record_tests.rs compares these rows as a signal
# on the adapter they name (its `frame-record` lines are these rows, and
# `frame-record: moved:` names a frame drawn otherwise); since
# ORACLE-ADAPTER (2026-10-26) the verdict is each frame's CPU twin, decided
# on any adapter, and a moved row fails nothing.
# Columns: arch, adapter, frame, WxH, SHA-256 of the RGBA bytes.
